## Datasets & cleaning

Currently there is the following datasets downloaded from SunNet:

```{r}
dir_info("data/raw/")
```

-   LinkAlter: is the data of connections between alters $i,j$ as reported by node $k$ but it does not include the links from $k,i|k,j$.
-   Alter and Ego are node level attributes from the survey, but they differ in detail. Ego info is more rich, all questions answered. Alter info is as perceived from the Ego, not all questions available.
-   `EGO_ALTER_CLEANED_ONLY PEER` contains the full survey.

```{r warning = FALSE, message=FALSE}
## links: 
link_alter <- read_csv("data/raw/Original Datase_linkAlter_All observations.csv")
alter <- read_csv("data/raw/Original Dataset_Alter_All observations.csv")
ego <- read_csv("data/raw/Original Dataset_Ego_All observations.csv")
mat <- read_csv("data/raw/Original dataset_EGO_ALTER_CLEANED_ONLY PEER.csv")

coords <- read_csv("data/raw/Coordinates_others cleaned EGO.csv")
```

```{r}
# rename:
names(link_alter) <- names(link_alter) |> 
    str_remove_all("networkcanvas") |> 
    str_replace(pattern = "uu", replacement =  "_") 

link_alter <- link_alter |> 
    rename(link_id = `_id`) 

# net <- link_alter |> # 3410
#     select(source_id, target_id) |> 
#     bind_rows(link_alter |> select(source_id = ego_id, target_id = source_id) |>
#                   unique() ) |> #3950
#     bind_rows(link_alter |> select(source_id = ego_id, target_id) |> unique()) |> # 4490
#     unique() |> # 3975
#     network(directed = TRUE, matrix.type = "edgelist", ignore.eval = TRUE)

df_mat <- mat |> 
    select(source = idencuesta,  target = idal, ego_id = networkcanvasegouuid, alter_id = networkcanvasuuid) 

df_alters <- link_alter |> 
    filter(connectionalter == 1) |> 
    select(ego_id, alter_id = source_id, target_id) |> 
    left_join(df_mat) |> 
    rename(ego_old = ego_id, ego_id = alter_id, alter_id = target_id) |> 
    select(-ego_old)

df_edges <- bind_rows(df_mat, df_alters) |> 
    filter(!is.na(source), !is.na(target)) |> 
    unique()

df_nodes <- df_edges |> 
    pivot_longer(cols = c(source, target), names_to = "role", values_to = 'node_id') |> 
    pivot_longer(cols = c(ego_id, alter_id), names_to = "roles", values_to = "alias") |> 
    select(node_id, alias) |> 
    unique()

net <- network(
    df_edges |> select(source, target) |> unique(), 
    directed = TRUE, matrix.type = "edgelist", ignore.eval = TRUE
)


plot.network(
    net, displayisolates = TRUE, edge.col = alpha("grey50", alpha = 0.4), vertex.col = "orange",
    vertex.border = 0, edge.lwd = 0.01)

```

Extract the node and edge list to create attributes:

```{r}
nodes <- tibble(node = network.vertex.names(net)) |> 
    # id is the id in the network object, node_id is the id in the database (df_nodes). node_id is need to merge with attributes.
    rownames_to_column("id") |> 
    mutate(id = as.numeric(id)) |> rename(node_id = node)
edges <- as.edgelist(net)

edges <- edges |> as_tibble() |> 
    rename(source = V1, target = V2) |> 
    mutate(source = as.numeric(source), target = as.numeric(target))

edges <- edges |>
    left_join(nodes, by = c("source" = "id")) |> 
    rename(source_id = node_id) |> 
    left_join(nodes, by = c("target" = "id")) |> 
    rename(target_id = node_id)
edges
```

Node attributes: `ego` and `altitude` don't exist on the dataset

Function to chose the opinion of the majority:

```{r}
# function for the majority

x <- c("Mantenido", NA, "Mantenido","Sembrado", NA)

majority <- function(x){
    if(length(x) == 1 | all(is.na(x))) 
        return(NA)
    else
        tbl <- table(x) |> sort(decreasing = TRUE)
        return(names(tbl)[1])
}

majority(c(NA, NA, NA))
```

```{r}
# alters
alters <- mat |> select(node_id = idal, starts_with("shadealter"), starts_with("alterferti"), starts_with("altervillage"), leader, name, ) |> 
    mutate(sex = genero(name)) |> 
    mutate(sex = case_when(

    mutate(shadechanges = case_when(

        shadealter_5 == TRUE ~ NA,
        shadealter_6 == TRUE ~ NA,
        shadealter_7 == TRUE ~ NA
    )) |> select(-starts_with("shadealter")) |> 
    mutate(fert_org = case_when(
        alterferti_1 == TRUE ~ TRUE,
        alterferti_2 == TRUE ~ FALSE,
        alterferti_3 == TRUE ~ NA,
        alterferti_4 == TRUE ~ NA
    )) |> select(-starts_with("alterferti")) |> 
    mutate(village = case_when(
        altervillage_1 == TRUE ~ "1",
        altervillage_2 == TRUE ~ "2",
        altervillage_3 == TRUE ~ "3"

    arrange(node_id) |> 
    group_by(node_id) |> #filter(node_id == 59)
    summarize( # variables with [1] are not unique, selecting first value
        leader = any(leader), name = unique(name)[1], sex = unique(sex),
        shadechanges = majority(shadechanges),
        fert_org = any(fert_org), village = unique(village)[1]
    )
```

## Modelling

From now on the script is improved to isolate repetition and separate data manipulation from modeling per se.

Load data and libraries:
```{r}
load("data/network_cleaned.Rda")
library(sna)
library(network)
```

Most models are done for a subnetwork for which we have complete data. Before we selected as the actors with age (egos), but now we want to control for geographic distance, so we need to include only people with coordinates.

```{r}
# this was made by Maria, don't know why (well recover the id from nodes)
node_attrs <-  node_attrs |> left_join(nodes)

## select subnetwork (we don't need the edge list again)
subnet <- get.inducedSubgraph(net, v = which(!is.na(net %v% "lon")) ) 

# e is an index of nodes of the subnetwork
keep_order <- tibble(
    node_id = subnet %v% "vertex.names"
) |> rownames_to_column(var="order")


# Y is the response vector in the regressions: structural changes
Y <- node_attrs |> 
    right_join(keep_order) |> arrange(order) |> ## preserving order of network
    mutate(shadechanges = case_when(
        shadechanges == "Sembrado" ~ 3,
        shadechanges == "Disminuido" ~ 1,
        .default = 2
    )) |>
    pull(shadechanges)

# X is a matrix of covariates
X <- node_attrs |> ungroup() |> 
    right_join(keep_order) |> arrange(order) |>
    mutate(intercept = 1) |> 
    select(intercept, training_shade, village, education, age, sex, leader, tspecies) |>
    mutate(
        village = as.numeric(village),
        sex = case_when(sex == "male" ~ 0, .default = 1),
        education = case_when(
            education == "none" ~ 0, education == "primary" ~ 1,
            education == "secondary"~2, education == "superior" ~ 3,
            .default = 0),
        training_shade = as.numeric(training_shade)
    ) |> 
    as.matrix()
```

For modelling purposes, we will use `W1` and `W2` as matrix covariates that control for variables of interest. 

`W1` in **Model 1** (Model presentation to Selva August 2025)
Weighted by Frequency that people see each other. We select only 3 & 4 values. And then normalize. The normalization is by row so at the end it sums one. I will illustrate with an example: If a person has two contact, one with 3 and another with 4, so the normalization is doing the following: 3+4=7 Then. 3/7=0.043  4/7=0.57

```{r}
W1_matrix  <- as.matrix.network.adjacency(subnet, attrname = "frequency") 
W1_matrix[!(W1_matrix %in% c(3, 4))] <- 0  #only 3 & 4 values.
W1_norm <- W1_matrix / rowSums(W1_matrix) #normalize the network
W1_norm[is.na(W1_norm)] <- 0
```

`W2` is the matrix of distance between people:

```{r}
library(sf)
pnts <- tibble(node_id = subnet %v% "vertex.names") |> 
    left_join(nodes |> select(node_id, lon = Longitud, lat = Latitud))
pnts <- st_as_sf(pnts, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
w2 <- st_distance(pnts, by_element = FALSE)
```

Now we can isolate cleanly the model steps and make sure that across models the same data is entering the formulas:

### LNAM 

Fit the model: 
```{r}
fit1 <- lnam(y = Y, x = X, W1 = W1_matrix, W2 = w2)
summary(fit1)
```
**Model 2**. Weighted by Frequency Only with 3 &4, and living 3 and 4 like that. No normalization. 

```{r}
W1_matrix  <- as.matrix.network.adjacency(subnet, attrname = "frequency") 
W1_matrix[!(W1_matrix %in% c(3, 4))] <- 0 

fit2 <- lnam(y = Y, x = X, W1 = W1_matrix, W2 = w2)
summary(fit2)
```

**Model 3**. Weighted by Frequency. Only considers 3 & 4 options of more strongest ties, and we give them both a value of 1. No normalization

```{r}
W1_matrix  <- as.matrix.network.adjacency(subnet, attrname = "frequency") 
W1_matrix[!(W1_matrix %in% c(3, 4))] <- 0  #only 3 & 4 values.
W1_matrix[W1_matrix %in% c(3, 4)] <- 1 #give value of 1 to 3& 4 values
W1_matrix[W1_matrix != 1] <- 0  

fit3 <- lnam(y = Y, x = X, W1 = W1_matrix, W2 = w2)
summary(fit3)
```

**Model 4** is not weighted:

```{r}
W1_matrix <- as.matrix.network.adjacency(subnet) 

fit4 <- lnam(y = Y, x = X, W1 = W1_matrix, W2 = w2)
summary(fit4)
```

**Model 5** Weighted by the amount of people connected. More people, less value.

```{r}
adj <- as.matrix.network.adjacency(subnet, matrix.type = "adjacency") 
row_sums <- rowSums(adj) ##normalize the matrix
row_sums[row_sums == 0] <- 1 
W1_matrix <- adj / row_sums

fit5 <- lnam(y = Y, x = X, W1 = W1_matrix, W2 = w2)
summary(fit5)
```

**Model 6.** (Model suggested by Angela in Oct. 2025) Weighted by Frequency that people see each other. We select only 3 & 4 values and give them a value of 1. And then normalized. The normalization is by row normalization is based on the total of ties, not only the number of strong ties.

```{r}
freq_mat <- as.matrix.network.adjacency(subnet, attrname = "frequency")
strong_mat <- freq_mat
strong_mat[strong_mat %in% c(3, 4)] <- 1
strong_mat[!(strong_mat %in% c(1))] <- 0  # everything else 0
total_ties <- freq_mat
total_ties[total_ties > 0] <- 1
row_sums <- rowSums(total_ties)
row_sums[row_sums == 0] <- 1
W1_matrix <- strong_mat / row_sums
W1_matrix[is.na(W1_matrix)] <- 0

fit6 <- lnam(y = Y, x = X, W1 = W1_matrix, W2 = w2)
summary(fit6)
```
**Model 7** (strong and weak ties)

```{r}
weak_mat <- as.matrix.network.adjacency(subnet, attrname = "frequency")
strong_mat <- as.matrix.network.adjacency(subnet, attrname = "frequency")


strong_mat[strong_mat %in% c(3, 4)] <- 1
strong_mat[!(strong_mat %in% c(1))] <- 0  # everything else 0
weak_mat[weak_mat %in% c(1, 2)] <- 1
weak_mat[!(weak_mat %in% c(1))] <- 0

W1_matrix <- strong_mat / row_sums
W1_matrix[is.na(W1_matrix)] <- 0
W2_matrix <- weak_mat / row_sums
W2_matrix[is.na(W2_matrix)] <- 0


fit7 <- lnam(y = Y, x = X, W1 = W1_matrix, W2 = W2_matrix)
summary(fit7)

```
**Model 8.** Emotions (same model 6 of frequency)
Model suggested by Angela in Oct. 2025, but with emotions. 
Weighted by emotions. We select 1 as strong, and 2, 3, 4, 5 as weak. So we only selec values of 1. And then normalized. The normalization is by row so at the end it sums one.The normalization is based on the total of ties, not only the number of strong ties.

```{r}
freq_mat <- as.matrix.network.adjacency(subnet, attrname = "close")
strong_mat <- freq_mat
strong_mat[strong_mat %in% c(1,2)] <- 1
strong_mat[!(strong_mat %in% c(1))] <- 0  # everything else 0
total_ties <- freq_mat
total_ties[total_ties > 0] <- 1
row_sums <- rowSums(total_ties)
row_sums[row_sums == 0] <- 1
W1_matrix <- strong_mat / row_sums
W1_matrix[is.na(W1_matrix)] <- 0


fit8 <- lnam(y = Y, x = X, W1 = W1_matrix, W2 = w2)
summary(fit8)

```
**Model 9** (like the three but with emotions)
Weighted `W1` by Frequency. Only considers 1 options of more strongest ties. No normalization

```{r}
# this line had "emotions" in attrname, throwing error
W1_matrix  <- as.matrix.network.adjacency(subnet, attrname = "frequency") 
W1_matrix[!(W1_matrix %in% c(3, 4))] <- 0  #only 1 values.
W1_matrix[W1_matrix %in% c(3, 4)] <- 1 #give value of 1 to 3& 4 values
W1_matrix[W1_matrix != 1] <- 0  

fit9 <- lnam(y = Y, x = X, W1 = W1_matrix, W2 = w2)
summary(fit9)
```

### ERGMs

Exponential random graph models explore the generative process of the network by modeling link formation, the probability of a link.
It is not sufficient to explore network diffusion / network influence.
But if the behaviour we want to test is adoption of shading or organic fertilizing, and it is socially diffused, the prob of links should be higher between people with such attributes, and stronger (e.g. edge weight).

```{r}

```
